scenes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: revised visual proposal, one 16:9 pixel-art adventure-game exterior.
Primary request: Transform the reference's small craft forge into a convincing MECHANIZED INDUSTRIAL IRON FOUNDRY in the London industrial district, around the 1840s. Reference is only for the existing game's rich crisp pixel art, amber sunset, readable adventure camera and straw-hat protagonist. Create a substantially new industrial plant silhouette, not a cottage with added chimneys.
Composition: one full-frame landscape 16:9 elevated three-quarter adventure view. Large soot-stained brick foundry hall spans the upper 60 percent, elongated pitched roofs with glazed ridge monitors, riveted iron framing, repeated tall arched industrial windows glowing from the furnaces, three tall narrow brick smokestacks. A substantial iron-trussed receiving bay at center-right shows shadowed overhead chain hoist and stacked mould flasks. Next to the bay a distinct normal-sized wooden pedestrian door reinforced with iron at ground level, lit by two small amber lanterns, unmistakable entrance for the hero. Important: the building and machines are larger than the previous cottage while still sized to a single playable screen.
Visible industrial production clues: a low brick engine house on the far right with exposed large flywheel and guarded shaft under a canopy; iron pulley and a horizontal line shaft at loading bay, no modern machinery. On far left a hand-operated iron jib crane unloading pig-iron bars from a low wagon; narrow industrial wagon rails confined to the loading strip beside the facade. Grouped stacks of heavy ingots, mould flasks, casting sand boxes, coke bunker and compact work carts at edges. Equipment drawn in believable hand-forged iron construction, no ornamental steampunk complexity.
Keep the lower 35-40 percent as a generous unobstructed cobblestone walking yard. Open lane at far left leads back to the district; center forecourt accessible to entrance. Background distant London roofs and smoky chimneys under a golden sky. Dark charcoal iron, warm weathered red brick, orange furnace highlights; pixel clusters, crisp outlines, rich tactile small detail matching reference, NOT smooth digital painting, NOT photorealism.
ONE straw-hat chibi hero near lower center-left, cream shirt, brown vest and trousers, full height around 8 percent of frame height; same sprite proportions as reference. No other people, no HUD, no text, no sign lettering, no arrows, no puzzle panels, no modern electric motors, no hydraulics, no vehicles from the twentieth century, no futuristic factory, no giant blast furnace tower, no mine lift. A believable 1840s industrial foundry scene with strong readable mechanical character.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: revised visual proposal, one 16:9 pixel-art adventure-game interior.
Primary request: Reimagine the reference's artisanal room as the INTERIOR OF A MECHANIZED INDUSTRIAL IRON FOUNDRY AND FORGING HALL in London around the 1840s. Use reference ONLY for crisp warm pixel art, scene camera, straw-hatted hero and Cort's equal character height. The new room is recognizably industrial, with several powered workstations, not a blacksmith cottage.
Composition: ONE full-screen landscape 16:9 cutaway game scene, slightly elevated near-frontal adventure view. Soot-blackened red brick hall with high iron-and-timber roof trusses and tall arched factory windows. Keep a wide continuous stone walking aisle across the LOWER THIRD; every machine is set behind that aisle, never blocking traversal. Human-size exit door at far left opens onto the warm cobblestone forecourt.
Three clear production zones across the rear two-thirds. LEFT: compact brick and riveted-iron cupola melting furnace with a visible orange tapping opening and a small iron ladle beneath it, moulding beds and sand casting flasks immediately beside it, everything behind a low iron curb. CENTER: brick reheating furnace with hot iron billets on the hearth; overhead a period iron traveling chain hoist carrying an EMPTY casting ladle over the rear work area, believable iron roof girder and visible chain, not over the hero's walking aisle. RIGHT: an unmistakable Nasmyth-style EARLY STEAM HAMMER, two dark iron uprights, large vertical steam cylinder at top, straight piston rod and hammer head over an anvil block; driven by steam pipe from side wall, no hydraulic hoses. The whole hammer is roughly three chibi-character heights tall, impressive but fits the room.
Along the upper rear wall a visibly coherent horizontal iron LINE SHAFT on bearings, two pulleys and broad leather belts descending to a compact rolling mill at far rear right. Visible large flywheel behind it; machinery constructed from plain riveted cast iron, manual levers and simple steam pipes, NOT dense decorative steampunk gears. At middle rear a practical mould-making bench with few tools and iron bars. A modest water trough along the right wall. Material storage along edges only, no giant foreground vat.
For scale only, TWO small chibi sprite figures on the clear foreground aisle: straw-hatted hero at lower left-center and moustached Cort at lower center-right. BOTH EXACTLY THE SAME head/hat-to-sole pixel height, 8 percent of frame height, same cute large-head body proportions. Cort has rolled cream sleeves, dark burgundy shirt accents, brown leather apron; no giant muscular adult. Both stand away from molten metal and moving machinery, not actively forging. Pixel art characters readable against floor.
Warm white-orange furnace light, scattered warm lanterns, cool muted window light, dark iron and red brick. Match reference's polished dense handcrafted pixel clusters; sharp sprite-like shapes, clear mechanical silhouettes. No text, HUD, labels, arrows, puzzle UI, no small craft fireplace as main feature, no modern hydraulics, electrical cabinets, yellow modern safety stripes, glass skyscrapers, giant cathedral interior or photorealistic people. This is a standalone playable-scene concept, not a diagram or collage.
